extracted.intended_audience: inventors and entrepreneurs (particularly in Georgia/Georgia Tech community) seeking patent and trademark filing assistance
extracted.subtask_description: A university library resource guide listing programs, contacts, and eligibility notes for inventor and entrepreneur assistance with patent and trademark filing (registered practitioners, pro bono, pro se, law clinics, and business development resources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized practitioner requirement (USPTO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only registered patent attorneys and agents are authorized to practice in patent matters before the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locate registered patent attorneys and agents through the 'Find A Patent Practitioner' database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Pro Bono assistance (eligibility/apply)
rubrics_metrics.description: If qualified, you may also apply for patent Pro Bono assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For State of Georgia, contact 'Georgia Patents' for further information; video resources on how to apply to the USPTO Patent Pro Bono Program are linked from the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Law School Clinic Program participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO's Law School Clinic Program allows you to connect to a participating law school student who may help you with your patent and trademark filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program participation can provide student-attorney assistance for filings; the guide links to the USPTO Law School Clinic Program for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Pro Se Assistance Program (support for independent filers)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO's Pro Se Assistance Program provides patent assistance to independent inventors and business owners and helps them increase the quality of pro se applications and assist pro se applicants with making informed decisions regarding their patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact via Email: innovationdevelopment@uspto.gov; Phone: 1-866-767-3848. The program is intended to raise the quality of pro se filings and inform applicants of options.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Inventor and Trademark Assistance Centers (contact points)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO's Inventor Assistance Center and Trademark Assistance Center provide assistance and can be contacted for help.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact phone for both centers: 1-800-786-9199. Use these centers as centralized USPTO help resources for inventor/trademark questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use bar associations to identify practitioners in good standing
rubrics_metrics.description: Local or national Bar associations are reliable sources for identifying a practitioner in good standing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed: Atlanta Bar Association, State Bar of Georgia, American Bar Association. These organizations can help verify credentials and standing of attorneys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider inventor assistance programs if filing pro se due to cost
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent process is complex as it relates to a set of laws, regulations, policies and procedures. If you decide to file a patent application on your own due to cost concerns, consider using these inventor assistance programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide aggregates programs (USPTO Pro Se Assistance, Pro Bono, Law School Clinics, Inventor Assistance Center) to help independent filers improve application quality and make informed decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product and business development resources for inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: Need additional assistance in product/business development? The guide points to local and regional resources to support commercialization and business development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources listed include Advanced Technology Development Center (ATDC) at Georgia Tech, Georgia Minority Business Development Agency (MBDA) Business Center, Small Business Development Centers (SBDC) at GSU, KSU, UGA, and the USPTO IP Identifier. These are recommended complements to legal assistance when developing or commercializing an invention.
